title: A Hollow-Knight-tight movement kit at 60 Hz: coyote time is exactly six ticks, the dash is exactly five flat metres, the air dash stays spent until touchdown, and the jump cut halves the rise
binding: One flat document at simulation.rateHz 60 with a deck, a wall and a floor 20 m below, and ONE kit authored entirely in today's action vocabulary. The measurement discipline is the point: NOTHING here presses a button on a schedule. A scripted body.press lands on whatever tick the console pump happens to drain on, so every number this proof pins is instead either a settled fixed point or a per-body counter that a kit onFact trigger advanced on exact simulation ticks. coyoteTicks counts the airborne ticks on which Recently(Grounded, 0.1s) still held; riseTicks counts Rising ticks; dashSpentTicks counts airborne ticks with the air charge at zero; the dashes fire from Grounded-edge and Airborne-edge triggers, which are clocked by the body's own facts, not by stdin. world.wait therefore only has to be LONG ENOUGH, never exact, and a loaded host's catch-up burst cannot move a verdict. The positive leg establishes, tick-exactly: coyote time is 6 ticks at 60 Hz for an authored 0.1 s window (the forcing world's own target number); a PlanarImpulse of speed 25 for 0.2 s moves the body exactly 5.00 m and exactly flat — pos goes from (0.00, 0.03, 0.00) to (5.00, 0.03, 0.00), zero vertical and zero lateral drift; the air dash fires once (airDashFires 1), is spent for 68 of the fall's 69 airborne ticks, and its charge is back at 1 the tick the body grounds (requested=0 effective=1 — resetFact Grounded is the restore-on-contact mechanism); the coyote-gated jump fires once through the real Recently(Grounded, 0.1s) gate; and ScaleVerticalVelocity 0.4 fired on the third Rising tick cuts the rise to 11 ticks. world.kits echoes shaping=response(engage=instant release=instant) — 'acceleration: instant' is spelled by OMITTING the rate — and a second kit in the same document carries the jetpack shape the vocabulary does admit, jet:Lift(rise=28 fall=46)[thrust=1] with a fuel spend row. The discriminating leg runs the SAME script against discriminating.world.json, whose ONLY differences are the authored coyote window (0.05 s instead of 0.1 s) and the removal of the jump-cut trigger. If coyoteTicks were a constant rather than the authored window converted to ticks, or if ScaleVerticalVelocity did not really shorten the rise, the two legs would read identically. They do not: coyoteTicks falls 6 -> 3, exactly linear in the authored seconds, and riseTicks rises 11 -> 24 with cutFires 1 -> 0.
